import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 7

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)
-/

namespace Erdos7

open Set

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_7 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∀ i,
      ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos7

reformulations.difference: The source asks for finitely many congruences with distinct odd integer moduli greater than 1. Lean instead uses StrictCoveringSystem ℤ and requires each modulus ideal not to be contained in Ideal.span {2}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every integer ideal has a unique nonnegative generator n. The covering-system fields supply finitely many cosets covering ℤ, exclude the zero and unit ideals, and require distinct ideals, corresponding to distinct moduli n > 1. The coset {a} + (n) is exactly the congruence class a modulo n. Furthermore, (n) ≤ (2) iff 2 divides n, so its negation is precisely oddness. Conversely, any finite distinct odd covering with moduli greater than 1 packages into this structure. The explicit non-top conjunct is redundant because CoveringSystem already supplies it. The full equivalence with a Fin k-indexed numerical formulation was proved as Erdos7Review.actual_iff_numeric in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean; its axioms contain no sorryAx.

review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and its supporting definitions. The outer answer(sorry) correctly represents the existential yes/no question. The source still records the general odd-moduli problem as open, matching the category; its solved odd-squarefree variant is a different claim. Lean checks excluded empty and singleton index types, tested zero/unit and small moduli, and constructed a standard distinct covering system to confirm the underlying structure is satisfiable.
